# Changelog — hello-retail-rest-api

What changed in each released version of the plugin, written for the person who installs it.
Update with `/plugin marketplace update helloretail`, then `/reload-plugins`.

**Do not edit this file.** The Release workflow writes it. Entries are added in the PR that
makes the change, as a new file under `changelog.d/` — see the README there for the format,
and `CLAUDE.md` → "Release notes" for the house style. On merge the workflow folds those
fragments into the version it publishes.

## 1.1.7 — 2026-10-28

### Changed

- `pages-api` now explains how to paginate: `products.count` caps how many products a response
  returns, and `products.start` steps through them (`start: 0` then `start: 20` for pages of 20).
  `products.start` is optional and defaults to `0`; it was listed as required.

- `cart-tracking-api` no longer treats an HTTP 500 as a server error to report to support. Like
  the other skills, it now says the generic `UNEXPECTED ERROR` body can also mean bad input, so
  check the request first.

### Fixed

- `recommendations-api` now documents `count` as required on Unmanaged recommendation requests;
  it was listed as optional, which led to requests built without it.
- `pages-api` no longer claims only `url` and `key` can fail a request. It now lists every input
  that returns an HTTP 500: a misspelled `format` or `deviceType`, a malformed `trackingUserId`,
  and a relative `url` without its leading slash.

- `troubleshooting-with-hello-retail-mcp` now filters a config's audit-log history by
  `sequenceKey`. It said `sourceId`, which returns only one version of a recommendation box or
  Pages config, not its full history.

## 1.1.6 — 2026-10-27

### Added

- `search-api`, `recommendations-api` and `pages-api` explain how to find every native product
  property and its exact name: send one request without a `fields` array and read them off the
  response.

### Changed

- `troubleshooting-with-hello-retail-mcp` now explains `apiLogTag`, the query-string parameter
  every endpoint accepts for tagging requests so they can be found in the API log with
  `onlyTagged`. `recommendations-api` no longer covers it, because the parameter is not specific
  to Recommendations.

### Fixed

- `click-tracking-api`, `search-api` and `recommendations-api` now say that leaving out the
  `fields` array returns every available property, `trackingCode` included, on every endpoint.
  Previously they said `trackingCode` only came back when listed in `fields`.
- `search-api`, `recommendations-api` and `pages-api` now say that an empty `fields` array returns
  an empty object for every result, so it is not a way to ask for every property.
- `search-api` now states that the zero-result products in `zeroResultContent` always carry every
  available property, whatever `products.fields` lists, and no longer describes their field names
  as different from the requested ones.
- `pages-api` no longer tells you to request `isOnSale` rather than `onSale` in `products.fields`.
- `recommendations-api` and `pages-api` now say, as `search-api` already did, that a property only
  has to be mapped in the ETL for `fields` to return it; Data fields indexing is needed only for
  filtering and sorting.
- `search-api`'s example request now asks for the product image as `imgUrl`; it previously used
  `image`, which is not a product property.

## 1.1.5 — 2026-10-26

### Changed

- `search-api`, `recommendations-api`, `pages-api` and the four tracking skills now state that Hello Retail's REST endpoints have no rate limiting to consider, instead of listing rate limits as unknown. `search-api` still warns against excessive requests, such as a search box without debouncing that sends one request per keystroke.
- `view-tracking-api`, `cart-tracking-api`, `conversion-tracking-api`, `customer-id` and `troubleshooting-with-hello-retail-mcp` now name the API log filter for each endpoint (`collect_pageview`, `collect_cart`, `collect_conversion`, `collect_customerid`), so a log check can be narrowed to that endpoint's requests.

## 1.1.4 — 2026-10-21

### Fixed

- `pages-api` no longer ties `params.filters` to the Pages config's product conditions. Any
  field indexed in Data Fields can be used for per-request rules such as the forwarded category
  id; static rules such as "sale products only" ideally go in the product conditions instead.

## 1.1.3 — 2026-10-20

### Changed

- `cart-tracking-api` and `conversion-tracking-api` now state that the endpoints work on any
  platform, and that the automatic tracking on Shopify, Magento 2 and Shopware is a Hello Retail
  SDK feature that requires the SDK on the frontend. A customer on those platforms without the
  SDK on the frontend handles cart and conversion tracking through the REST API.

## 1.1.2 — 2026-10-20

### Changed

- `search-api` now specifies that changing the search query clears every applied filter and the
  selected sort, both in the next request and in the UI, so filters chosen for one query never
  silently narrow the next one.

## 1.1.1 — 2026-10-19

### Changed

- `pages-api` now states that the request's `url` can be absolute or relative, and recommends the
  relative path (`/category/snowboards`): it is exactly what Hello Retail requires, while the part
  before it in an absolute URL can be misinterpreted. Its examples now send the relative path.

### Fixed

- `pages-api` now sets `firstLoad` by whether a request can change the scope of products, not by
  whether it is the page's first request. Applying or removing a filter sends `true`; a sort
  change or going to the next page sends `false`.

## 1.1.0 — 2026-10-16

### Added

- `customer-id` connects a shopper's `trackingUserId` to the shop's own customer id through the REST API, so a logged-in shopper's phone and laptop share one personalization profile without the Hello Retail SDK.
  It covers when to send the call, consent, and the `id` field name, which otherwise fails with an HTTP 500.

## 1.0.3 — 2026-10-07

### Fixed

- `pages-api` no longer tells you to send `firstLoad: false` on a request that changes filters; it
  stays `true` so the filter panel's counts refresh, and only pagination or re-sorting sends `false`.
- `pages-api` examples now always request `trackingCode`, so tiles built from them can be
  click-tracked.
- `recommendations-api` now points to the MCP tools for reading and changing a Managed box's
  algorithm and filters, instead of saying this can only be done in the dashboard.
- `cart-tracking-api` and `conversion-tracking-api` now agree that both endpoints store nothing for
  an opted-out shopper, and the link between them works.

## 1.0.2 — 2026-09-30

### Changed

- The plugin is renamed from `hello-retail-unmanaged` to `hello-retail-rest-api` and now shows as
  "Hello Retail (REST API)"; its skills are invoked as `/hello-retail-rest-api:<skill>`.
  Existing installs stop updating: uninstall `hello-retail-unmanaged@helloretail`, then run
  `/plugin install hello-retail-rest-api@helloretail` (and update `enabledPlugins` if you set it
  in `settings.json`).

## 1.0.1 — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- `recommendations-api` names the current tool for listing a website's recommendations when
  checking whether a box exists to reference by `key`.

## 1.0.0 — 2026-09-18

### Added

- `search-api`, `recommendations-api` and `pages-api` document the public content endpoints for
  a custom frontend: request and response shapes, config states, filters and sorting, and the
  rule that a shopper-facing filter needs a configured filter on the config or Design, not just
  an indexed field.
- `click-tracking-api`, `view-tracking-api`, `cart-tracking-api` and `conversion-tracking-api`
  cover the four collect endpoints, including which of them the Hello Retail SDK already handles
  for you and which it never does — getting that wrong silently double-counts or drops events.
- `tracking-user-id` is the single place the `hello_retail_id` convention lives: minting one
  when no SDK is on the page, caching it, the 24-zero opted-out sentinel, and the races that
  make a `trackingUserId` go missing. Every other skill links here instead of repeating it.
- `troubleshooting-with-hello-retail-mcp` points an integration that "isn't working" at the API
  log and audit log before it re-reads its own request code. It needs Hello Retail's MCP server
  connected in the same client, which installing this plugin does not do on its own.
